context: Give both paths an explicit hold they honour, and evaluate the newly added gate rather than the base-ref copy on synchronize, so a gate added mid-flight applies to PRs already open.
description: auto-merge-on-open.yml re-arms auto-merge on synchronize using the base-ref copy of its predicate, and nightly.yml runs green_unmerged_sweep.py --apply, so gh pr merge --disable-auto is undone by the next push or the next night. Draft status is the only durable hold, because both paths skip drafts. This is not theoretical: #1528 auto-merged without the owner review #1529 had just added, because a follow-up push re-armed it while the base-ref predicate was still the pre-#1529 copy.

preserves.behavior: Auto-merge still arms by default for ordinary PRs; this adds a hold, it does not disable the feature
Drafts continue to be skipped by both paths
Evaluating the PR copy of a predicate must not let a PR weaken its own gate
The gate machinery stays self-protecting - a change to it still requires review
